page.title: Page headline, shown in capitals with a letter-by-letter ignite. Keep it short (≤ 12 characters ideal).
intro.paragraph: A playful 'fantasy' metaphor for web development (portals = websites, realms = users, grimoires = learning resources). Keep the tone whimsical; the words reveal one by one as the reader scrolls.
projectsCard.unit: Sits beside a large number (the count). English never changes form, but use your language's plural forms.
projectsCard.ariaLabel: Screen-reader name of a clickable card. It must contain the card's visible words in the same order (eyebrow, number + unit, legend, 'View progress') so voice-control users can say them.
projectsCard.srPrefix: Prefix of a live-region announcement; the change sentence follows directly after it. Keep the trailing space (or your language's equivalent separator).
statsCard.title: {name} is the GitHub account's display name (a person's name, never translated).
languagesCard.percent: <n></n> is replaced by an animated number. Move it to wherever the number goes relative to the % sign in your language (e.g. Turkish '%<n></n>').
skillsCard.count: <n></n> is an animated count; the noun after it agrees with {count}.
skillsCard.popover.slash: Separator between the public and private repository counts.
progress.age.minutes: Compact elapsed time, e.g. '2m 04s ago'. {m} and {s} are numbers already formatted; keep it very short.
progress.ringLineOne: First of two stacked lines inside a small ring ('board items' / 'done'). Each line must stay very short (≈ 12 characters).
wire.span: A date range: {start} and {end} are already-formatted dates or the word for 'Present'.
changes.dot: Separator between independent change sentences in one banner.
changes.pipe: Separator between independent change sentences in one banner.
changes.languages.rank: {rank} is the new position in the ranking; '#' here is a literal number sign.
changes.repo.stars: {direction} is 'increased' or 'decreased' — inflect the verb as your language needs.
changes.skills.entry: {name} is a technology name (untranslated); {category} is a translated category heading.
progress.columns.todo: Name of a column on a GitHub Projects (kanban) board, shown as a tiny uppercase legend label next to a count. Use the term the target language uses for this workflow stage in project-management tools (as GitHub/Jira localise it). Very short (1-3 words).
